record.paper_title: Advances in periodic difference equations with open problems
record.original_question: For commuting continuous interval maps f0, f1: I → I, determine the set Per([f0, f1]) of least periods of periodic orbits of the alternating system x_{n+1} = f_{n mod 2}(x_n). In particular, decide whether every period pattern realized by the noncommuting examples from Theorem 2.1 can also be realized by a commuting pair.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.2. Find Per([f0, f1]) for commuting maps f0, f1 ∈ C(I). More precisely, can the examples of Theorem 2.1 be constructed such that f0 and f1 commute?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $I=[0,1]$ and let $C(I)$ denote the set of continuous self-maps of $I$. Given an ordered pair $(f_0,f_1)$ with $f_0,f_1\in C(I)$, consider the non-autonomous (2-periodic) discrete dynamical system
$$x_{n+1}=f_{n\bmod 2}(x_n),\qquad n\ge 0.$$
A point $x\in I$ is called periodic of least period $p\ge 1$ for this alternating system if $x$ is fixed by the $p$-fold composition along the alternating sequence and is not fixed by any shorter such composition; here, if $p$ is odd, the $p$-fold composition is understood as $f_{(p-1)\bmod 2}\circ\cdots\circ f_1\circ f_0$ (and analogously for the shifted starting index). Define
$$\mathrm{Per}([f_0,f_1])\subseteq\mathbb{N}$$
to be the set of least periods of periodic orbits of the alternating system.

Assume in addition that $f_0$ and $f_1$ commute, i.e. $f_0\circ f_1=f_1\circ f_0$.

(a) Characterize all subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ that arise as $\mathrm{Per}([f_0,f_1])$ for some commuting pair $f_0,f_1\in C(I)$.

(b) For every set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ known to be realizable as $\mathrm{Per}([g_0,g_1])$ for some (possibly non-commuting) pair $g_0,g_1\in C(I)$, decide whether $S$ is realizable by a commuting pair.
artifact.category_tag: Periodic structure of alternating interval maps
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of describing Per([f_0,f_1]) for commuting continuous interval maps is listed as an open problem in the literature on periodic difference equations. Related work (e.g., on periodic structure of alternating interval maps, dynamics of compositions of commuting interval maps, and a converse result for commuting affine circle maps) addresses adjacent settings but does not resolve the commuting interval-map case. No source found that fully settles the question.

status_evidence.title: Periodic structure of alternating continuous interval maps
status_evidence.snippet: Studies periodic structure of sequences generated by alternating two continuous interval maps.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework of Per([f_0,f_1]) for general (not necessarily commuting) continuous interval maps.

status_evidence.title: On the dynamics of composition of commuting interval maps
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates dynamics arising from compositions of commuting continuous interval maps.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial results on commuting interval maps but does not characterize Per([f_0,f_1]).

status_evidence.title: A converse result concerning the periodic structure of commuting affine circle maps
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes period sets in the commuting affine circle map setting.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves an analogous problem for affine circle maps, leaving the interval case open.
